section_summary: This section documents U.S. State Department, interagency, and Far Eastern Commission deliberations between late 1947 and early 1949 regarding policy for the replacement of cultural property lost or destroyed during Japanese aggression. It highlights intense debate between the Department of State and the Department of the Army over the legality, equity, and diplomatic wisdom of restitution in kind under Article 56 of the 1907 Hague Convention. Additionally, the section covers a formal Japanese Government petition and subsequent interdepartmental discussions concerning the return of thirty National Treasure and Important Art Object swords mistakenly surrendered to American occupation forces.

subfiles.about: A memorandum reporting on the discussions and actions of the Far Eastern Commission Reparations Committee meeting held on April 21, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Reports on Far Eastern Commission discussions concerning cultural object replacement, accessory plant removals, patents, reparations claims, occupation costs, neutral assets, and repatriated Japanese funds.
subfiles.title: Reparations Committee Meeting of April 21

subfiles.about: A memorandum forwarding a proposed amendment from Chinese Ambassador Wellington Koo regarding the restitution of cultural objects to China.
subfiles.summary: Transmits an amendment suggested by Chinese Ambassador Wellington Koo regarding Japanese cultural object replacement, recommending SANACC resolve interdepartmental disagreements.
subfiles.title: Restoration of Cultural Objects to China

subfiles.about: A Far Eastern Commission paper circulating a tentative United States policy proposal regarding the replacement of lost cultural objects.
subfiles.summary: Circulates a tentative United States policy proposal requiring Japan to replace lost or destroyed cultural objects with items of substantially equivalent character.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects: Tentative United States Proposal (C1-272)
subfiles.to: Committee No. 1: Reparations, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: A Far Eastern Commission subcommittee report presenting majority and minority draft policies and a United States statement on replacing lost cultural objects.
subfiles.summary: Transmits majority and minority draft policies on replacing cultural objects lost during Japanese aggression, along with a United States statement explaining its position against compensating private losses.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects: Report of Subcommittee (C1-272/1)
subfiles.to: Committee No. 1: Reparations, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: A statement by the Chinese Delegation arguing against limiting cultural object replacement to property that previously served public purposes.
subfiles.from: Chinese Delegation to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Argues that restricting cultural restitution to objects that served public purposes is unsound and unworkable, urging broader replacement of cultural treasures lost to Japanese aggression.
subfiles.title: Chinese Statement on Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects (C1-272/2)
subfiles.to: Committee No. 1: Reparations, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: A memorandum circulating the Civil Affairs Division member's objections to proposed policies for replacing cultural objects in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Circulates Civil Affairs Division objections to cultural object restitution in kind, citing administrative difficulties and political friction in Japan, and recommending referral to SANACC.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan) (SFE 202/2)
subfiles.to: State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East

subfiles.about: A Department of State charge slip recording the tracking and borrowing of documents relating to cultural object replacement.
subfiles.summary: Records file loans and document transfers concerning correspondence between the Secretary of State and Secretary Royall.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip (894.403/6-848)

subfiles.about: A letter informing Secretary Royall of a revised State Department policy proposal on replacing cultural objects lost to Japanese aggression.
subfiles.summary: Informs Secretary Royall that State has revised its cultural replacement policy to address Army and Theater Commander objections.
subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of the Army Kenneth C. Royall Regarding Cultural Replacement Policy

subfiles.about: A letter transmitting a revised draft policy statement and draft telegram to General MacArthur on Japanese cultural object replacement.
subfiles.summary: Charles E. Saltzman explains the State Department's narrowed policy on cultural object replacement, designed to satisfy Allied claims without depleting Japan's heritage or violating Article 56 of the Hague Regulations. The enclosed policy statement establishes a three-member specialist board in Tokyo to evaluate claims for identical or closely similar items. An accompanying draft telegram addresses General MacArthur's and General Clay's legal, administrative, and political objections.
subfiles.title: Letter to General G. L. Eberle Regarding Cultural Objects Replacement Policy with Enclosures

subfiles.about: A letter requesting reconsideration of cultural object replacement proposals in view of Army, MacArthur, and Clay objections.
subfiles.summary: Requests reconsideration of cultural replacement proposals, arguing that seizing Japanese cultural objects violates the Hague Convention and sets dangerous precedents.
subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of State George C. Marshall Regarding Replacement of Cultural Objects

subfiles.about: A letter responding to Secretary Royall's concerns about U.S. working papers in the Far Eastern Commission and defending cultural replacement.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that U.S. working papers in the Far Eastern Commission did not commit the government, while maintaining that cultural replacement warrants consideration.
subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of the Army Kenneth C. Royall Regarding FEC Working Papers and Cultural Replacement

subfiles.about: A letter reiterating Department of the Army objections to cultural object replacement under Article 56 of the Hague Convention.
subfiles.summary: Reasserts that seizing Japanese cultural objects violates Article 56 of the Hague Convention, rejects a neutral commission, and urges adhering to established policy.
subfiles.title: Letter to Under Secretary of State Robert A. Lovett Regarding Cultural Objects Replacement Policy

subfiles.about: A letter transmitting the State Department Legal Adviser's opinion on Article 56 of the Hague Convention.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the State Department Legal Adviser's opinion affirming the legality of cultural replacement under the Hague Convention, requesting Draper's comments.
subfiles.title: Letter to Under Secretary of the Army William H. Draper, Jr. Regarding Legal Aspects of Cultural Replacement

subfiles.about: A legal opinion analyzing whether requiring Japan to replace lost or destroyed cultural objects violates Article 56 of the 1907 Hague Convention.
subfiles.summary: Concludes that Article 56 of the 1907 Hague Convention does not prohibit requiring Japan to replace destroyed cultural objects, citing historical precedents from Versailles and World War II treaties.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Cultural Objects Removed or Destroyed by the Japanese

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum expressing disagreement with the proposed cultural replacement policy and questioning Far Eastern Commission competence.
subfiles.summary: Criticizes the proposed cultural replacement policy as unsound and likely to cause bitterness, questioning Far Eastern Commission competence.
subfiles.title: U.S. Policy on Replacement of Cultural Objects Lost or Destroyed as a Result of Japanese Aggression

subfiles.about: A memorandum suggesting formal consultation with the War Department before replying to Tokyo regarding surrendered Japanese art swords.
subfiles.summary: Recommends obtaining formal War Department comment on Tokyo's despatch regarding Japanese art swords and revising the draft instruction's arguments.
subfiles.title: Return of Japanese Swords

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting a Japanese Government petition and inventory requesting the return of historic and National Treasure swords surrendered to Allied forces.
subfiles.summary: William J. Sebald transmits a request from SCAP's Civil Information and Education Section and the Japanese Government for State Department assistance in recovering historic Japanese swords improperly surrendered to American military personnel. The enclosed Japanese inventory details thirty National Treasure and Important Art Object swords surrendered across multiple prefectures, including celebrated blades by Masamune and other master smiths. The accompanying petition asks SCAP to locate and return these valuable cultural objects to their rightful owners under SWNCC 322 procedures.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 727: Return to Japan of Swords Classified as Objects of Art, with Enclosures

subfiles.about: A letter requesting the views of the Department of the Army on Tokyo Despatch 727 concerning surrendered Japanese art swords.
subfiles.summary: Requests Army views on Despatch 727, noting State's view that tracing surrendered Japanese art swords would be expensive and impractical.
subfiles.title: Letter to Assistant Secretary of the Army Tracy S. Voorhees Regarding Return of Japanese Swords

subfiles.about: A memorandum requesting a legal opinion on whether SWNCC 322 applies to surrendered Japanese swords alleged to be art objects.
subfiles.summary: Requests the Legal Adviser's opinion on whether SWNCC 322 applies to recovering surrendered Japanese swords classified as art objects.
subfiles.title: Applicability of SWNCC 322 to Despatch No. 727 on Japanese Swords

subfiles.about: An office file copy of a memorandum recommending formal War Department consultation regarding surrendered Japanese swords.
subfiles.summary: Recommends obtaining formal War Department comment on Tokyo's despatch regarding Japanese art swords and revising the draft instruction's arguments.
subfiles.title: Return of Japanese Swords (Office Copy)

subfiles.about: A memorandum reporting that informal Army inquiries indicate opposition to attempting the recovery and return of Japanese art swords.
subfiles.summary: Reports that informal Army discussions show Plans and Operations and Civil Affairs divisions oppose returning surrendered Japanese art swords as impractical.
subfiles.title: Return to Japan of Swords Classed as Objects of Art

subfiles.about: A legal opinion concluding that surrendered Japanese swords of artistic value were wrongfully taken cultural objects under SWNCC 322.
subfiles.summary: Concludes that artistic swords surrendered under general disarming orders constitute cultural objects wrongfully taken within the meaning of SWNCC 322.
subfiles.title: Are Japanese Swords Cultural Objects Wrongfully Taken, Within Meaning of SWNCC 322

subfiles.about: A letter declining to examine legal intricacies of cultural replacement and referring the issue back to Marshall and Royall.
subfiles.summary: Declines to examine legal intricacies of cultural replacement, stating Secretary Royall prefers discussing the matter directly with General Marshall.
subfiles.title: Letter to Assistant Secretary of State Charles E. Saltzman Regarding Cultural Replacement Legalisms

subfiles.about: A file copy of Charles E. Saltzman's letter requesting Army views on Tokyo Despatch 727 regarding surrendered Japanese art swords.
subfiles.summary: File copy of letter soliciting Army views on Despatch 727 and noting the impracticality of recovering surrendered Japanese swords.
subfiles.title: Letter to Assistant Secretary of the Army Tracy S. Voorhees Regarding Return of Japanese Swords (File Copy)

subfiles.about: A memorandum arguing against efforts to recover thirty surrendered Japanese swords due to militaristic symbolism, Allied reaction, and impracticality.
subfiles.summary: Recommends against recovering thirty surrendered Japanese art swords, citing militarist symbolism, potential Soviet propaganda, recipient good faith, and administrative difficulties.
subfiles.title: Tokyo's Despatch No. 727 on Return to Japan of Swords Classified as Objects of Art
